newsitem.title: UK: Rolls Royce says to sell Bristol Aerospace.
newsitem.headline: Rolls Royce says to sell Bristol Aerospace.

text.p: Rolls Royce Plc said on Monday it intends to sell its Canadian Bristol Aerospace Ltd subsidiary.

"Over a period of time, Bristol Aerospace's products have gradually moved away from the business areas that Rolls Royce sees as central to its operation in the next century," Stan Todd, president of Rolls Royce Industries Canada Inc said.
Todd said in a statement this had reached a point to where it was in the best interests of the business for it to be owned by a company "more focused on these products."
"This will allow Bristol to remain competitive and continue its long history as a major force in the Canadian aerospace industry," he added.

Bristol Aerospace, which employs 960 people, specialises in the repair and overhaul of fixed and rotary wing aircraft, the manufacture of aero-engine and aircraft components for Rolls-Royce and other manufacturers and the production of missiles and rockets for military and space applications.

Rolls-Royce said it plans to proceed with the sale as soon as possible but in the meantime it would "continue to support and encourage Bristol in its work and ensure that all commitments and contracts, both external and internal, are honoured".
